sampling_model.design: For each analyst-selected \(s\), the assignment law is chosen from all outcome-independent probability distributions on \(\{0,1\}^{2J}\); after pair-preserving symmetrization it is represented by \(q\in\Delta(\mathcal N_J)\).
sampling_model.units: The \(2J\) labelled units and all binary potential outcomes are fixed; only the partition into \(J\) pairs is observed before assignment, while armwise discordance is latent.
sampling_model.treatment: A binary assignment \(A\) is the only source of randomness, and \(Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{jr}=A_{jr}Y_{jr}(1)+(1-A_{jr})Y_{jr}(0)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No marginal positivity restriction is imposed; zero-mass assignment and observation cells are handled by closed quadratic perspectives and explicit primal completions.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no sampled nuisances. Nature chooses a fixed schedule in the sensitivity class \(\Theta_{J,s}\); risks, optimal procedures, and confidence sets are reported separately as \(s\) varies.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Given an assignment vector and an invariant estimator, uniform randomization over the permutation group is minimax under invariant states and a quasiconvex objective.
The mixed-strategy optimal design minimizes worst-case variance of difference in means over a structured conditional-mean class and may require randomization over several partitions.
For unrestricted binary potential outcomes, Bernoulli assignment with a nonlinear posterior-mean rule attains the all-procedure minimax risk, whose second-order term is governed by the Airy function.
Independent assignment remains minimax over all measurable estimators for unrestricted bounded potential outcomes, with an endpoint-supported least-favourable problem.
Within stratified designs treating half of every stratum, matched pairs formed by the prognostic index minimize the mean-squared error of difference in means.

For a fixed stratified experiment with unbiased and uncorrelated group-CATE estimators, homoscedastic outcomes, and group CATEs bounded by \(B\) outcome standard deviations, Theorem 2.1 derives the lowest worst-case-MSE estimator among linear combinations of those group estimators.
The Gram--Schmidt Walk design controls a covariance-based balance--robustness trade-off and yields MSE and asymptotic inference guarantees for Horvitz--Thompson estimation.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population totals, the minimax bound is attained if and only if inclusion indicators are pairwise independent.
Under within-pair coin flips, the worst compatible binary attributable-effect allocation is a single boundary corner and exact inversion needs logarithmically many binomial tails.
Exact binary ATE intervals under balanced Bernoulli or matched-pair assignment can be computed with \(O(\log n)\) randomization tests.
Exact conservative stratified binary ATE inference can be obtained by maximizing randomization \(p\)-values over compatible potential-outcome tables.

body.tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-specified sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction with a joint assignment--observation coefficient yields an exact finite conic game, an \(O(J^{20})\)-entry rectangular rational kernel, and a dual certificate for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; a rational \(J=2,s=1\) instance rules out every paired--Bernoulli mixture. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while at and above the threshold the leading term leaves a measure-valued face. The central open result is the exact smaller-order selection of limits of finite minimizers, including the critical approach to \(\rho=1/2\). The same corrected kernel gives a finite-sample confidence-set sensitivity family for correlated optimal laws.

project_justification.gap: Published minimax results justify paired assignment under prognostic superpopulation structure, independent assignment under unrestricted bounded schedules, or linear shrinkage under a fixed stratified design with observed groups and bounded group CATEs. They do not solve the intermediate fixed-population sensitivity class indexed by a latent armwise pair-discordance cap while jointly choosing the design and an arbitrary measurable estimator, and they do not distinguish first-order-optimal laws from limits of exact finite minimizers.
project_justification.niche: The sensitivity restriction breaks full unit exchangeability without treating unobserved potential-outcome discordance as pretreatment information. It leaves a finite but nontransitive observation experiment in which correlated assignment laws and nonlinear posterior-mean estimators can be jointly optimal.
project_justification.fill: For every selected \(s\), the project supplies the correctly normalized assignment-marked orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk sensitivity frontier, a first-order measure face, the exact-minimizer selection problem, and exact randomization-test inversion.

body.related_work: Bai2023WhyRandomize establishes the group-averaging principle and identifies approximate invariance and joint design--estimator choice as a boundary; its theorem is used as a symmetry template rather than a target to beat. Kallus2021Optimality shows that structured minimax design can require a mixed strategy, but its precision criterion fixes difference in means. SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes solve the unrestricted bounded all-estimator problem by symmetries that do not preserve separate armwise pair-discordance sensitivity classes; Proposition 2 recovers their binary endpoint. Bai2022MatchedPairs obtains matched-pair optimality inside stratified half-treatment designs under a superpopulation precision criterion, which informs the low-sensitivity endpoint but does not make both-arm discordance observable. deChaisemartin2022Shrinkage, Theorem 2.1, derives minimax-linear shrinkage of observed group-CATE estimators under a bound on group CATE magnitudes. Its formal problem fixes the stratified design and observed groups and optimizes only over linear estimators, whereas this project imposes latent armwise within-pair outcome discordance and jointly optimizes the assignment law and every measurable estimator; it therefore informs the bias--variance motivation but is not a theorem-level target. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 controls a covariance-based balance--robustness frontier for Horvitz--Thompson estimation and informs the assignment-measure geometry. AronowLopatto2026 gives an independence frontier under design unbiasedness, while the present comparison permits biased nonlinear estimators. Wilson2026MatchedBinary, Zhang2026FastBinaryCI, and LiSpertusStark2025 inform exact inversion; their product or fixed-stratum mechanisms do not cover correlated noncanonical laws or an analyst-indexed latent mismatch class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A corrected checker formed \(K_{hno}\) from the joint assignment-marked coefficient and verified \(\sum_oK_{hno}=1\) for every \((h,n)\) at all \(J=2,3,4\) and \(0\le s\le J\). The resulting schedule-orbit counts are \((10,38,55)\), \((20,96,184,220)\), and \((35,195,454,650,715)\); the largest full rectangular array has \(7{,}668{,}375\) entries at \(J=4,s=4\), consistent with \(O(J^{20})\). The recomputed minimax risks by increasing \(s\) are \((0,0.0904264890,0.1030826943)\) for \(J=2\), \((0,0.0584446250,0.0719156622,0.0756571245)\) for \(J=3\), and \((0,0.0414059556,0.0546757329,0.0591555795,0.0601329999)\) for \(J=4\). Projected second-order-cone coordinate optimization reproduces the all-mixed singleton at \(s=0\), broad faces at the unrestricted endpoints, and the strict noncanonical \(J=2,s=1\) instance; the critical grids \(J=2,s=1\) and \(J=4,s=2\) have materially different finite coordinate-range patterns. Because these finite critical cases do not establish a stable sequence law, Open-ended Question 6 remains at its stated resolution. Only the \(J=2,s=1\) separation is backed by exact rational inequalities; the other displayed risks and face diagnostics are numerical early-kill checks, not theorem contributions.
body.honest_scope: The parameter \(s\) is an analyst-selected sensitivity index for latent both-arm discordance, not a practitioner-known or administratively verifiable quantity. Every risk, optimal face, asymptotic regime, and confidence set is conditional on the selected value or sequence, so substantive reporting varies \(s\) rather than selecting it from observed outcomes. The corrected finite orbit representation, endpoint reductions, rational noncanonical separation, first-order value, low-sensitivity concentration, high-sensitivity first-order envelope, and exact inversion are theorem obligations. The complete limit set of exact finite minimizers for \(\rho\ge1/2\) is the principal open object. At \(s=0\) the problem reduces to exact paired recovery; at \(s=J\) it reduces to the unrestricted Bernoulli nonlinear minimax experiment of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 and Hull2026BoundedOutcomes.
